## Derivation of the Exponential TDM Survival Formula

This section derives the formula for cumulative egg-to-fry survival (S) over \\(n\\) days under the **exponential TDM model**.

$$
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr)
$$

#### 1. Instantaneous Mortality (Hazard) Rate

Assume that at water temperature \\(T\\) (in °C), the instantaneous daily mortality rate (hazard) is an exponential function of temperature:

$$
h(T) \;=\; \alpha \, e^{\beta\,T},
$$

where:
- \\(\alpha > 0\\) is a baseline mortality coefficient.
- \\(\beta\\) controls how sharply mortality increases with temperature.

#### 2. Survival over a Small Interval

In continuous-time hazard theory, the probability of surviving a small time interval \\(\Delta t\\) when the hazard is \\(h\\) is \\( \exp(-h \cdot \Delta t) \\). Taking \\(\Delta t = 1\\) day, daily survival at temperature \\(T\\) becomes:

$$
\exp\bigl(-h(T)\bigr) \;=\; \exp\bigl(-\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T}\bigr).
$$

#### 3. Survival Over Multiple Days

If each day \\(i=1, \dots, n\\) has temperature \\(T_i\\), and survival across days is independent, the total survival is the product of daily survivals:

$$
S \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{n} \exp\bigl(-\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\bigr).
$$

#### 4. Final Form

Using the identity \\(\prod e^{x_i} = e^{\sum x_i}\\), with \\(x_i = -\alpha e^{\beta T_i}\\), the product collapses into a single exponential of the summed hazards:

$$
\boxed{
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha\,e^{\beta\,T_i}\Bigr)
}.
$$

## Derivation of the Linear Threshold TDM Survival Formula

This section derives the formula for cumulative survival (S) under the **linear threshold TDM model**.

$$
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\alpha \sum_{i=1}^{n} \max(T_i - \beta,\,0)\Bigr)
$$

#### 1. Define the Daily Hazard Rate

Under this model, mortality only occurs above a thermal threshold \\(\beta\\). The hazard rate on day \\(i\\) is proportional to the "excess" temperature above this threshold:

$$
h_i = \alpha \cdot \max(T_i - \beta,\,0)
$$

where \\(\alpha\\) scales how strongly excess temperature drives mortality. If \\(T_i \le \beta\\), the hazard is 0.

#### 2. Survival Over One Day

The probability of surviving a single day with hazard \\(h_i\\) is:

$$
\exp(-h_i) \;=\; \exp\bigl(-\alpha \cdot \max(T_i - \beta, 0)\bigr).
$$

#### 3. Multiplying Over All Days

Assuming independence, survival over \\(n\\) days is the product of daily survivals:

$$
S \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^n \exp\bigl(-\alpha\,\max(T_i - \beta,0)\bigr)
$$

#### 4. Final Form

Again, using the identity \\(\prod e^{x_i} = e^{\sum x_i}\\), the final closed-form expression is the exponential of the summed daily hazards:

$$
\boxed{
S \;=\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\alpha \sum_{i=1}^{n}\max(T_i - \beta,\,0)\Bigr)
}.
$$
